The elements listed are:
- Cs (Cesium): An alkali metal in period 6
- Fr (Francium): An alkali metal in period 7 (the last period)
- H (Hydrogen): In period 1
- Li (Lithium): An alkali metal in period 2

In general, electronegativity:
1. Increases from left to right across a period
2. Decreases from top to bottom down a group

All of these elements except hydrogen are in Group 1 (alkali metals). Among alkali metals, electronegativity decreases as you move down the group. Therefore, francium (Fr), being the lowest element in Group 1, would have the lowest electronegativity among the alkali metals.

Hydrogen has a moderate electronegativity (around 2.2 on the Pauling scale), which is higher than the alkali metals.

The order of electronegativity from lowest to highest among these elements would be:
Fr < Cs < Li < H

Therefore, francium (Fr) has the lowest electronegativity among the given options.
